name: Look Atlas
tagline: Premium AI product photography with reusable AI Directors for fashion, jewelry, and ecommerce
description:
Look Atlas is an AI product-photography studio for fashion, jewelry, and ecommerce. You start from a product photo and a reusable AI Director for lighting, styling, and framing, then add close-ups for embroidery, fabric, a jewelry setting, or hardware. The same direction is meant to produce on-model shots, campaign frames, and lifestyle scenes. People searching the brand are usually asking what a month costs. The pricing page is more specific than the homepage.

lookatlas.com/pricing was fetched twice on 16 Nov 2026. Both responses were HTTP 200, both files were 748,584 bytes, and the files matched. The final URL was www.lookatlas.com/pricing. The page title is "Pricing — AI Product Photo Shoots from $49/mo". A yearly control is labeled "2 MONTHS FREE". The HTML prints one set of prices. It does not print a discounted yearly dollar amount, so this listing does not invent one.

Starter is $49 a month: 80 credits, about 40 photos, products on lifelike AI models, a limited model library, full commercial rights on every photo, and failed shoots auto-refunded. The card also lists AI product videos and human touch-ups, with no count for either. One version of the card says "Try the studio on your own catalog." Another on the same page says "Individual sellers & small brands."

Pro is $99 a month: 200 credits, about 100 photos, 20 human touch-ups a month, and credits that can also pay for videos and AI models. Extended model library. 2K quality. Everything in Starter. This is the first plan that numbers the retouches and says the credit pool is shared with video.

Business is $399 a month: unlimited photos at priority speed, unlimited 4K, 100 human touch-ups a month (unlimited touch-ups on yearly), an extended library plus on-demand models, 600 credits for videos and AI models, and priority support from a person. Everything in Pro. The header says a flagged shot goes to a human retoucher who fixes it within 48 hours.

Credit math uses the page's own "about" figures. 80 credits for about 40 photos, and 200 credits for about 100 photos, are both about 2 credits a photo. If you use the whole allowance, Starter is about $1.23 a photo ($49 / 40) and Pro is about $0.99 ($99 / 100). Those divisions are not a rate card the page prints. Business does not meter photos. Video and AI models on that plan come out of a separate 600-credit pool. Unlimited photos is not unlimited video.

Every card ends with "Start Free Shoot." The pricing HTML does not say how many images that includes, whether they are watermarked, what resolution they are, or whether a card is required. A free shoot is not a published quota.

Commercial use is on every paid card as "full commercial rights on every photo." Failed generations are auto-refunded. The footer links a Shopify app, free tools, and pages for AI fashion photography, ghost mannequin, clothing mockups, and jewelry. Support is support@lookatlas.com. The FAQ asks about hidden fees, plan changes, whether unused credits roll over, small brands, commercial use, how unlimited photos work, enterprise pricing, and what a touch-up is. Those answers were not in the fetched text. This listing does not guess. It does not claim credits roll over.

No founder name is on the pricing page. No Stripe-verified revenue page was found, so no revenue is stated. No API or MCP server is named there. An agent cannot spend these credits from the docs read today.

Best for a seller who knows the monthly photo count and will look at the files. About 40 photos, and no counted retoucher, is the $49 plan if the page's "about 40" holds. 2K, 20 human fixes, and video from the same credits is the $99 plan. 4K plus a retoucher on a 48-hour flag is the $399 plan. Extra Starter months do not become unlimited 4K.

Watch out for Starter listing videos and touch-ups that only Pro quantifies. Watch out for Business "unlimited" stopping at photos, with video capped at 600 credits. The yearly label says two months free while the HTML still shows $49, $99, and $399. The free-shoot button has no printed allowance. A 48-hour retouch is not a same-day campaign. "Full commercial rights" is the site's phrase, not a likeness-release opinion. Read the terms in the footer before you run an ad.

Alternatives here, and the job they actually do. PhotoAI (https://www.aiagentsinfo.com/directory/photoai) is Pieter Levels' tool for likeness portraits, headshots, and video. HeadshotPro (https://www.aiagentsinfo.com/directory/headshotpro) makes headshots from selfies, sold in packs. InteriorAI (https://www.aiagentsinfo.com/directory/interiorai) restyles a room. Midjourney (https://www.aiagentsinfo.com/directory/midjourney) is a general image generator and does not publish this catalog table. ColorCraft (https://www.aiagentsinfo.com/directory/colorcraft) builds KDP coloring books from $9 a month. None of them is a garment catalog with a human retoucher on a 48-hour flag.

Last verified: 16 Nov 2026.
